 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Jrue Holiday wanted his return to professional basketball in 2020 to mean something beyond his performance on the court. As the NBA prepared to resume its season during the COVID-19 pandemic, the New Orleans Pelicans guard and his wife, Lauren, decided to use his remaining salary to support communities affected by racial inequality.
 Following the murder of George Floyd and the protests that swept across the United States, Holiday committed the remainder of his 2020 NBA salary, approximately $5.3 million, to social justice causes. The decision established the Jrue and Lauren Holiday Social Impact Fund, which focused on supporting Black-owned businesses and nonprofit organizations.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The couple's commitment was especially significant because of the circumstances surrounding the NBA's return. Lauren, a former United States women's national soccer team star and two-time Olympic gold medalist, was pregnant with their second child. Holiday faced the difficult decision of leaving his family to compete in the Orlando bubble while the country confronted widespread social unrest.
 As WRTV reported on Holiday's decision to donate his NBA earnings , the fund was designed to direct financial assistance toward communities in Indianapolis, New Orleans and Los Angeles.
 Portland Trail Blazers guard Jrue Holiday (5) Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images
 The initiative supported Black-led nonprofits, small businesses and historically Black colleges and universities. Rather than limiting the commitment to a single organization, the Holidays wanted the money to reach grassroots groups working to create economic opportunities and address inequalities.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement WISH-TV also covered Holiday's decision to donate his remaining 2020 salary , highlighting how the basketball star planned to turn his earnings into support for social justice initiatives.
 The fund later expanded its reach to Milwaukee after Holiday joined the Bucks in a trade that year. That addition reflected the couple's commitment to supporting communities connected to their personal and professional lives.
 Holiday's decision demonstrated how professional athletes can use their financial resources and public platforms to support causes beyond sports. What began as a difficult decision to leave his family for the NBA season became a charitable commitment with a lasting community purpose.
